newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Elan Q1 directly marketed product sales up.
newsitem.headline: Elan Q1 directly marketed product sales up.

text.p: Elan Corporation Plc said on Wednesday that the proportion of directly marketed product sales exceeded 70 percent of total product sales in the first quarter, representing a fundamental transition of Elan's business.
Sales of products directly marketed by Elan were just eight percent of total product sales in the three months of 1996.
"The higher gross margins from these sales sustained a 30 percent increase in net income for the quarter," Elan chairman and chief executive officer Donal Geaney said in a statement.
Earlier, the drug delivery and biopharmaceutical company said net income in the three months to March 31, 1997 rose to $37.15 million from $28.62 million a year earlier.

Elan said product sales increased by 29 percent to $52.6 million in the first quarter, benefiting from sales of pre-launch quantities of Naprelan to the Wyeth-Ayerst division of American Home Products.
The first quarter results also included sales and earnings of Athena Neurosciences Inc, whose acquisition became effective from July 1, 1996.
Athena's first quarter sales included the launch of supplies of Zanaflex, the first product for the treatment of spasticity to be approved in the U.S. in over 20 years, in February, Elan said.
Geaney said that although it was too early to make any firm prediction as to Zanaflex's ultimate performance, Elan was very pleased with its reception by neurologists and patients to date.

He said he was also excited at the level of industry interest in Elan's platform of drug delivery and formulation technologies and expected that 1997 would see increasing interest in more new research agreements.
"I am optimistic about our prospects for the remainder of 1997," he said.
